Executive Summary
This manual defines how the course is audited, published, corrected and updated. It separates curriculum 
completion from file availability, verifies DOCX/PDF pairing, protects against broken downloads and duplicate 
content, and creates an update path that does not require unnecessary new volumes.
1. Quality Gates
Gate
Required check
Failure action
Content
Chapter sequence, scope and no 
unintended duplication
Correct source manuscript
Technical
Commands, configurations and 
examples are internally consistent
Revise and re-test
DOCX layout
Render every page; no clipping, 
broken tables or missing glyphs
Fix and re-render
PDF layout
Render and visually verify; selectable 
text and embedded fonts
Re-export and preflight
Pair integrity
Every DOCX has a matching PDF with 
the same stem
Regenerate missing pair
Links
Download and reference links resolve
Replace or annotate
Accessibility
Headings, table headers, readable 
contrast and meaningful link text
Apply safe fixes
Privacy
No sensitive metadata, credentials or 
private paths
Scrub before release
2. Current-Workspace Audit Scope
At build time, the active workspace contained 33 course DOCX files and 33 matching course PDF files. This count 
reflects files available in the current runtime, not the full historical library across previous conversations or 
storage locations.
Important distinction: Curriculum status may be complete while older files are not mounted in the current 
workspace. The included audit script reports file availability without incorrectly declaring missing historical 
files as unwritten content.
3. Automated File Audit
python scripts/audit_course_files.py --root /path/to/course-library --json-out audit.json
Checks:
- DOCX count
- PDF count
- DOCX files without matching PDFs
- PDF files without matching DOCX files

4. Release Naming Standard
DevOps_Master_Course_Volume_<NN><Part>_<Canonical_Title>_v<MAJOR>.<MINOR>.<PATCH>.docx
DevOps_Master_Course_Volume_<NN><Part>_<Canonical_Title>_v<MAJOR>.<MINOR>.<PATCH>.pdf
Examples:
DevOps_Master_Course_Volume_11B_Prometheus_PromQL_Alertmanager_v1.0.0.pdf
DevOps_Master_Course_Volume_14D_Model_Serving_RAG_Agents_LLMOps_v1.1.0.docx
5. Version Policy
Change

Example
Typo, broken link, formatting defect
PATCH

New lab, changed tool workflow, 
expanded chapter
MINOR
1.0.1 -> 1.1.0
Major restructure or incompatible 
learning sequence
MAJOR
1.1.0 -> 2.0.0
6. Errata Workflow
1.
Record the issue with volume, part, chapter, page and evidence.
2.
Classify severity: critical, high, medium or editorial.
3.
Verify the correction against authoritative documentation or reproducible tests.
4.
Update the source DOCX and companion repository asset.
5.
Render and visually verify DOCX and PDF again.
6.
Increment the version and update the changelog.
7.
Publish the corrected files and archive the replaced release.
7. Technology Update Cadence
Review
Cadence
Focus
Critical advisory review
As needed
Security, deprecations and broken 
workflows
Quarterly maintenance
Every 3 months
Links, versions and lab compatibility
Annual edition review
Once per year
Architecture changes, new standards 
and roadmap
Major curriculum review
Every 2-3 years
Structure, learning outcomes and 
market relevance
8. Update Decision Framework

Update an existing chapter when the learning outcome is unchanged.

Add an appendix or lab when a new tool is an alternative implementation.

Add a minor section when a new standard changes production practice.

Create a new part only when the topic requires a coherent multi-chapter learning track.

Create a new volume only when the domain is materially distinct and cannot fit the existing roadmap.
